assign.request: Critic B, the systems designer. Read the paging realm's code and docs (paging.js, readme.md, doc/*, every tree's page.js) and answer: what is the small handful of concrete building blocks this system actually has? Name at most six, each in one sentence a newcomer gets, and for each: is it shown by an example a newcomer can see; can a reader explore alternatives by configuring or generating; what in the realm is redundant with it or a synonym of it. Then the ten-line verdict: the handful, what to merge, what to delete, what is missing, and the one organizing principle the rebuilt realm should follow. Fix nothing.
assign.now: reading the brief and the realm's file tree
steps: read every tree's page.js (mechanisms, styles, sizes, toolbars, templates, transitions)
name the handful of blocks; map synonyms and redundancy
check each block for example + configurability

assign.now: read the whole realm - 6034 lines of js, 5 docs, 16 top dirs, 50 dirs total; mapping the blocks

log.msg: SCOPE READ: paging.js 528 + words.js 94 + samples.js 77 + demos.js 196 + baseline.js 181; doc/ = mechanisms 94, decisions 511, persistence 319, templates 199, builder 373; 16 top-level trees (build center critique doc examples explorer inventory made make mechanisms rightnav sizes styles templates toolbars transitions), 50 dirs, 6034 lines of js.

THE MODEL THE CODE ACTUALLY HAS: Paging = Page + a MODE (five one-word axes: style content layout mech toolbar) + a STAGE (toolbar, box, item rows, change caption). Everything else in the realm is a preset of those words or a second vocabulary for one of them.

BLOCK 1 STAGE - a bounded rectangle a click changes the inside of. Shown: yes (hub miniatures, mechanisms/swap four visuals on a fixed-height stage). Configure: NO - it has no chip and no word. Synonyms in code: $stage, paging-box, paging-shown, $frame, still(), templates-stage, paging-swapper-stage, build $screen/build-screen, tab panel. Nine names, one rectangle.

BLOCK 2 NAVIGATION - what a click on a child does, and how children are drawn. THREE vocabularies for one control: words.js MECHANISMS (launch expand swap takeover), make/tabs.js KIDS (columns tabs), build/words.js NAVS (none columns tabs rail rail-right takeover) which pairs kids+mech and is already the ruling in doc/builder.md. Plus transitions/ relabels the same axes FROM/BY/TO, templates/navigation restates the four again, inventory/ tabulates 16 realms by them, explorer/ points at the generator's own fifth vocabulary (wall list prose tabs vtabs), rightnav/ hand-builds rail-right as a separate Page subclass.

BLOCK 3 CONTENT - what is in the box. Four vocabularies: samples.js RUNGS xs-xl (ONE canned sample at five heights - a demo prop, not a block, and the axis the owner already read as a content switcher), templates families.js example() (11 real modules), build/words.js BLOCKS (prose cards template - data, the only real one), core generator's prose/list/wall. Only build/ lets a reader ADD content; everywhere else content is fixed.

BLOCK 4 ROOM - one width word for the box. words.js LAYOUT (center column wide full) is a RENAME of core's own words (default large fill full) and costs a translation table (TRACK in paging.js). full == takeover, admitted verbatim in examples/page.js ('the same word said twice'). center is not a width at all, it is an alignment, and it has both a top-level tree (center/) and a sub-page (sizes/center/).

BLOCK 5 ARRANGEMENT - where the parts sit around the box. FIVE vocabularies, none connected: words.js TOOLBAR (8 = 4 sides x inside/outside), build/words.js ARRANGES (4 layout numbers), build NAVS rail/rail-right, rightnav/ VARIANTS (width x side x placement), and /imagine/layouts/ which is a WHOLE SIBLING REALM of 17 layouts + 5 surfaces + 3 pad steps that paging only borrows four of. No page in the realm says these are one question.

BLOCK 6 SKIN - surface + type scale. The five surface words are written out THREE times: words.js STYLES, build/words.js SURFACES, imagine/layouts/system.js SURFACES (its comment even says 'paging's vocabulary'). families.js adds a fourth as TONE (wash surface prim dark). The type axis (compact regular display) lives only in templates/ and doc/templates.md already says moving it into words.js is four lines and deletes Template.Toolbar.

THIRTEEN VALUE-DIRECTORIES: styles/{plain card tint prim dark} + sizes/{center column wide full} + toolbars/{top left right bottom} are 13 modules that each demonstrate ONE value of one chip already switchable live on the parent. The want is real (a value deserves a url); the cost is not - one route() reading the word off the url replaces all thirteen.

NOT PAGING AT ALL, sitting in the realm: critique/ (19 realms shot and ranked - a site-wide layout audit, and its own paging row still reads 'Still a placeholder - Being built', i.e. stale) and inventory/ (a full-width table scoring 16 realms). Both are surveys of the SITE, not blocks of the system. explorer/ is 55 lines of prose about the core generator with two links - it is not an explorer, it is the owner's name for the thing that does not exist yet.

TWO EDITORS OVER ONE STORE: make/ (CRUD list, four word-chips a row, writes made/*/page.json) and build/ (seven controls, live stage, same store via make/made.js). build supersedes make's editing; make's list is the file manager. build/words.js NAVS + ARRANGES + BLOCKS is the best vocabulary in the realm and the only place a reader GENERATES a page from choices.

MISSING, measured against the owner's own words: (1) the two independent colour controls - today one word paints the box on 'card' and the whole column on the other four, which is his exact complaint; (2) any page that crosses layout x navigation x appearance x hierarchy - transitions/ is the closest and only crosses style x mech; (3) a library of preconfigured pages with a dropdown to switch; (4) a page inside a page ('put any one of these page types inside any other') - templates/ imports modules read-only into a box, nothing hosts a real page; (5) ext/drawer, which inventory/ itself names as the exact shape rightnav wants; (6) the stable-vs-dynamic label from the day's decision 5 - no page in the realm carries it.

VERDICT 1/10 - THE HANDFUL. Six words over one rectangle. STAGE: the bounded box a click changes the inside of, and which never moves. NAVIGATION: what a click on a child does, and how the children are drawn. CONTENT: what is in the box. ROOM: how much of the row the box gets, in one width word. ARRANGEMENT: where the page's other parts sit around the box. SKIN: the surface colour and the type scale.

VERDICT 2/10 - SHOWN BY AN EXAMPLE: five of six, yes, and several times over. The exception is the STAGE - it is the realm's own stated design rule and the one block with no page, no chip and no single name (nine in the code: $stage, paging-box, paging-shown, $frame, still(), templates-stage, paging-swapper-stage, build-screen, tab panel).

VERDICT 3/10 - EXPLORE BY CONFIGURING OR GENERATING: only in build/. Everywhere else the chips move two or three words of a fixed demo, and no page crosses two blocks - transitions/ is the single exception and crosses only skin x navigation. The owner's 'layouts x navigation x appearance x hierarchy' exists nowhere in the realm.

VERDICT 4/10 - MERGE, NAVIGATION: three vocabularies for one control. words.js MECHANISMS (4), make/tabs.js KIDS (2), build/words.js NAVS (6, which pairs the other two). Keep NAVS - doc/builder.md already ruled that navigation is ONE control - and delete the other two. rightnav/ then becomes the value 'rail-right' instead of a Page subclass with its own CSS and store key.

VERDICT 5/10 - MERGE, SKIN: the five surface words are written out three times (words.js STYLES, build/words.js SURFACES, imagine/layouts/system.js SURFACES) plus a fourth translation (families.js TONE). One list. Pull the type axis down from templates/ into it - doc/templates.md already costs it at four lines and says it deletes Template.Toolbar.

VERDICT 6/10 - MERGE, ARRANGEMENT: toolbar placement (8 words), build ARRANGES (4), build NAVS rail/rail-right, rightnav VARIANTS, and /imagine/layouts/ (17 layouts) are five vocabularies for one question. /imagine/layouts/ is the sibling realm that already owns it - paging should borrow it whole, not restate four of seventeen. Also merge the editors: build/ supersedes make/'s editing, make/'s list stays as the file manager over the one store.

VERDICT 7/10 - DELETE: critique/ and inventory/ (site-wide surveys, not paging blocks; critique's own paging row still reads 'Still a placeholder - Being built'), explorer/ (55 lines of prose about the core generator - the name is the owner's word for the thing that does not exist yet), center/ (an alignment, and sizes/center/ already exists), transitions/ (skin x navigation over five destination pages).

VERDICT 8/10 - DELETE, cont.: the 13 value-directories - styles/{plain card tint prim dark}, sizes/{center column wide full}, toolbars/{top left right bottom} - each a module demonstrating ONE value of a chip already live on its parent. The want (a value deserves a url you can send) is right; one route() reading the word off the url serves all thirteen. And delete the xs-xl content axis: it is one canned sample at five heights, the axis the owner already misread as a content switcher, and real content blocks (build's BLOCKS) replace it.

VERDICT 9/10 - MISSING: (1) two independent colour controls - today one word paints the box on 'card' and the whole column on the other four, the owner's exact complaint; (2) a combinator that crosses all six blocks at once, which is what 'explorer' was supposed to mean; (3) a library of preconfigured pages with a dropdown to switch; (4) a page hosted INSIDE another page - 'put any one of these page types inside any other'; (5) ext/drawer, which inventory/ itself names as the exact shape rightnav wants; (6) the stable/dynamic label from the day's decision 5 - no page in the realm carries it.

VERDICT 10/10 - THE ONE ORGANIZING PRINCIPLE: THE REALM IS ONE CONFIGURABLE PAGE, NOT A DIRECTORY OF PAGES. Six words, one stage, one control and one name each. Every directory that survives is a PRESET of those six words that earned a url - never a module that re-says a word. Today it is 16 trees and 50 directories saying six things; it should be one stage, six controls, and a library of presets you switch with a dropdown.

assign.outcome:
**The paging realm is six blocks wearing sixteen names.** Read-only audit of 6034 lines of js, 5 docs and 50 directories. Nothing under `public/imagine/` was touched.

**The handful** — one rectangle and six words over it: **stage** (the box a click changes the inside of, which never moves) · **navigation** (what a click on a child does, and how children are drawn) · **content** (what is in the box) · **room** (the width word) · **arrangement** (where the parts sit around the box) · **skin** (surface + type scale).

**Merge** — navigation is written three times (`MECHANISMS`, `KIDS`, `NAVS`); keep `build/words.js`'s `NAVS`, which already pairs the other two and is already the ruling in [doc/builder.md](/imagine/paging/doc/builder.md). The five surface words are written three times (`words.js`, `build/words.js`, `imagine/layouts/system.js`) plus a fourth translation. Arrangement is written five times, and [/imagine/layouts/](/imagine/layouts/) is the sibling realm that already owns it. `build/` supersedes `make/`'s editing.

**Delete** — `critique/` and `inventory/` (site surveys, not paging; critique's own paging row is stale), `explorer/` (prose, not an explorer), `center/`, `transitions/`, the 13 one-value directories under `styles/` `sizes/` `toolbars/` (one `route()` gives all thirteen a url), and the `xs`–`xl` content axis (one canned sample at five heights).

**Missing** — the two independent colour controls · a combinator crossing all six blocks · a library of preconfigured pages with a dropdown · a page hosted inside another page · `ext/drawer` · the stable/dynamic label.

**The one organizing principle: the realm is ONE CONFIGURABLE PAGE, not a directory of pages.** Six words, one stage, one control and one name each; every surviving directory is a preset that earned a url, never a module that re-says a word.
